Additionally, we presented results from a sensitivity study looking at different HTF compositions and assumed HTF hot temperature. NREL provided PowderMet, Inc. with an executable file of SAM that includes the ETES model developed in this project. Based on our analysis, PCMs within a salt slurry can increase TES energy density from around 200 kJ/kg to over 500 kJ/kg using salt slurries containing 36% by weight PCM. The higher energy density of the slurry leads to decreased TES tank sizes and costs. The salt slurries also increase the HTF-sCO temperature difference within the PHX, which decreases required PHX 2 conductance and hence cost. The bare erected cost for systems with salt slurries was found to be up to 40% cheaper than salt-only systems. Finally, using salt slurries with PCM can help maintain high HTF temperatures for the power cycle, increasing cycle efficiency. Within the results, we showed that the 1-tier PCM case presents the most favorable results; however, there are still many unanswered questions. To further improve this analysis, the following items should be addressed in future work: 1. Understand the engineering implications of adding PCM particles into a molten salt slurry, including but not limited to, density increase, flow characteristics, charging system design considerations, cost of the PCM material, and TES piping design. 2. Conduct detailed PHX design using higher fidelity modeling methods, i.e., computational fluid dynamics and finite element analysis. 3. Improve PHX cost estimates through a bottom-up cost analysis. 4.
